title: Module global sections correspond naturally to invariant stalks
statement: Let K be a field, Ks its separable closure, and Omega an algebraically closed algebraic extension of K containing Ks as a scalar tower. Let R be a commutative ring. Suppose E is an equivalence from etale R-module sheaves over Spec K to discrete R-linear Galois representations, i identifies its underlying-module functor with the geometric stalk at Omega, and i carries the Galois action on germs to change of lift by any extending automorphism of Omega. Then evaluation on the terminal etale object is naturally isomorphic, as an R-module functor, to E followed by invariants.

source.place: Tag 04JQ, lemma-equivalence-abelian-sheaves-point, scalar enhancement; Tag 04JM, lemma-global-sections-point

proof.text: Apply the set-valued sections-invariants theorem and compare the module stalk with its underlying set stalk using Point.sheafFiberCompIso. The comparison preserves germs. Every stalk element is represented by a germ; extend each Galois automorphism to Omega and use the two germ formulas to identify the two actions.

source.place: Tag 04JQ, lemma-equivalence-abelian-sheaves-point, scalar enhancement; Tag 04JM, lemma-global-sections-point

proof.text: Specialize the sections-invariants theorem to the bottom intermediate field, whose fixing subgroup is the whole group. Its etale spectrum is isomorphic to the terminal etale object by IntermediateField.botEquiv. Naturality of germ maps identifies the terminal germ with the bottom-field germ. Thus terminal sections map bijectively to fixed set-valued germs.

source.place: Tag 04JQ, lemma-equivalence-abelian-sheaves-point, scalar enhancement; Tag 04JM, lemma-global-sections-point

proof.text: Compose the linear terminal germ with i inverse and restrict its image to the invariant submodule. The two stalk comparison isomorphisms and the fixed-set bijection prove injectivity and surjectivity. Naturality follows from the terminal germ natural transformation and i inverse. These bijective linear components therefore give a natural isomorphism.
